candidates.statement: I. INTRODUCTION 13 This guidance provides updated recommendations for the format and content of a risk evaluation 14 and mitigation strategy (REMS) document for a prescription drug product, including a biological 15 drug product. 2 A REMS document, which is part of a REMS that is required by FDA, 16 establishes the goals and requirements of the REMS. 17 This guidance provides recommendations to applicants on drafting proposed REMS documents 18 and converting an already-approved REMS document to a new, standardized format that is 19 clearer, more informative, and supports submission of a REMS document in Structured Product 20 Labeling (SPL) format. FDA does not expect applicants of an approved product subject to a 21 REMS to submit a proposed REMS modification solely to convert their REMS document to the 22 new format. Changing the REMS document to the new format should be done in conjunction 23 with other REMS modifications. 24 This guidance provides an overview of the types of information that should be included in a 25 REMS document. Additional and more detailed information is provided in the template 26 appended to this guidance, which is also available on FDA’s Web site. 3 This guidance and the 27 appended template are intended to help ensure that REMS documents are clear, understandable 28 to stakeholders, and to the extent possible, consistent in content and format. 29

candidates.statement: III. FORMAT AND CONTENT OF A REMS DOCUMENT 98 A REMS document establishes the goals and requirements of the REMS as they relate to the 99 required REMS elements. This information is described in more detail in the sections below. 100 To facilitate the applicant’s implementation of the recommended format, FDA has developed a 101 template to use in conjunction with this guidance. The template is appended to this guidance and 102 is also available on FDA’s Web site, at 103 https://www.fda.gov/AboutFDA/Transparency/Basics/ucm325201.htm . 104 As described here, the template contains specific sections and provides standardized language to 105 describe common REMS requirements. The standardized language was developed by FDA after 106 review and comparison of existing approved REMS documents, consideration of stakeholder 107 feedback on REMS documents, and FDA’s experience in reviewing REMS and implementing its 108 REMS authorities. It is the Agency’s view that where REMS requirements are the same across 109 REMS, the language used to describe the requirements should be consistent. REMS Goals 118 The REMS Goals section should describe the overall, safety-related health outcome(s) that the 119 REMS is designed to achieve. Because risk mitigation goals cannot always be measured 120 directly, it is important to also include one or more intermediate measurable objectives that, if 121 achieved, indicate that the REMS is meeting its goals.
